description: Formation level profiles of the railways in the core box (scene x -1320..320, z -280..1200), taken from the OS London five-foot plan 1891-96: rail-level spot heights and bank-top readings where they exist, the ground beside the line where the OS draws no embankment hatching, and measured deck levels at bridges. scripts/railway_levels.py reads this register; scripts/build_infrastructure.py builds each railway's embankment, crossings and drawn level stations from it, and the landscape, bridge, yard and drainage builders read the built profile. Railways outside the box keep their earlier formation height.
frame: chainage: metres along the railway route as built in docs/data/infrastructure.json (the LT&SR on its retraced route below; the Woolwich branch after its existingBranchStart and Manor Road realignment), from its first point. offset: metres from the route, positive on the left of the direction of travel (normal (-uz, ux), south of the east-running LT&SR). Levels are scene y metres. A profile is a list [chainage, formation y, basis]; formation is the top of the earth bank (the bottom of the ballast); levels between points are linear.

railStack.evidence: The renderer stack (docs/infrastructure.js box helper; data/maps/east-depot-junctions.json branchJoin): ballast 0.24 m, rails from +0.33 m and 0.13 m deep, so rail top = formation + 0.46 m. A rail-level reading sets formation = reading - 0.46 m; a bank-top reading sets formation = reading.

atGrade.evidence: Explicit estimate. Where the OS draws no embankment hatching the formation sits on the ground: formation = the OS ground reading beside the line + 0.1 m, so the ballast top stands 0.34 m and the rail top 0.56 m above the ground (a ballast lift of 0.3-0.5 m). The ground is the OS reading, not the drawn model ground; where the two differ the register says so (groundComparison).

embankment.evidence: Measured on the OS five-foot plan: on the retraced LT&SR east bank (chainage 725-875, bank 2.2-3.5 m above the 7.5-7.9 ft foot) the hatching runs from the crest edge about 4.5 m out to toes about 10 m either side of the centreline, and south of the line by the gas works (chainage 120-280) to about 9.5 m: a side slope of about 1 in 1.75. The crest half-width (4.5 m) is the model's two-track formation. scripts/build_infrastructure.py and scripts/build_main_landscape.py draw the side slopes of the register railways at this slope down to the drawn ground, so the toe moves in and out with the bank height instead of standing at a fixed 15-17 m.

London, Tilbury and Southend Railway.routeEvidence: Retraced on the OS five-foot plan (scripts/factory_map_sources.py mosaic): east of Abbey Creek wharf the four drawn rails of the two running lines lie on one straight line (13 cross-sections from chainage 600 to 890, RMS 0.05 m about the line through scene (-2.8, 361.89) bearing (0.9287, -0.3707)). The prior trace ran along the southern slope hatching, 1.1 m south of the rails at chainage 600, 6 m at 700, 11.5 m at 800 and 15.1 m at 890. The route keeps its first four points (Bow Creek to Abbey Creek wharf, within 1.5 m of the drawn rails) and then follows that line across the bridge over the G.E.R. Woolwich branch and Manor Road to 15 m past its east abutment; the OS shows the line continuing east on embankment beyond.

London, Tilbury and Southend Railway, we.priorRoute: none: new route (task A, 5 October 2026); before it the LT&SR ended at a 17 m approach behind the Bow Creek west abutment, closed by an earth end (docs/railway-bridges.js lineEnds london-tilbury-and-southend-west)
London, Tilbury and Southend Railway, we.routeEvidence: Traced on the OS five-foot plan (scripts/factory_map_sources.py mosaic, zoom 18): the four drawn rails of the two running lines west of Bow Creek, read on cross-sections at x -605 (centre z 602.5), -700 (641.8), -770 (669.8), -800 (681.0) and -855 (697.0), run between the Steam Boiler Works (Fraser & Fraser, site 795) and St Leonard's Works (site 794) to the St Leonard's Street bridge, where the street crosses over the line, with Bromley Station beyond. The route starts at the end of the LT&SR approach (LT&SR station -16.8, on the line of its first segment, which the Bow Creek bridge follows and which lies about 3 m south of the OS centreline at the creek) and keeps that heading for 15 m, then joins the OS centreline by x -700 and follows it to x -834, 3 m east of the street's east kerb line on the OS. The line beyond, under the bridge and through Bromley Station, is not modelled: the street, the bridge and the station are not drawn here.
London, Tilbury and Southend Railway, we.evidence: London, Tilbury and Southend Railway from the Bow Creek bridge west through Bromley to the St Leonard's Street bridge, on the OS five-foot plan (1893-96). Two running lines. A separate record from the main LT&SR route so that the main route's chainages (bridges, controls, the Abbey Mills junction) are unchanged; it begins where the main route's west approach ends.
